won.giza.t: Khufu's tomb, built about 2584–2561 BC; the only ancient wonder still standing, though most of its casing is gone.
won.stonehenge.t: The sarsen circle on Salisbury Plain, dated about 2400 BC in the New7Wonders list.
won.ziggurat-ur.t: Stepped temple platform of the moon god at Ur, raised in the twenty-first century BC.
won.hanging-gardens.t: Described as built about 600 BC by Babylonians or Assyrians, at Babylon or perhaps Nineveh; no trace survives and their existence is unresolved.
won.temple-of-artemis.n: The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
won.temple-of-artemis.t: Built about 550 BC by Greeks and Lydians, burnt by Herostratus in 356 BC, rebuilt from 323 BC and plundered by the Goths in AD 262.
won.statue-of-zeus.n: The Statue of Zeus at Olympia
won.statue-of-zeus.t: Phidias's seated Zeus of 435 BC in the temple of 466–456 BC; carried to Constantinople and lost to fire in the fifth or sixth century.
won.parthenon.t: Athena's temple on the Acropolis, built in the fifth century BC (the Acropolis is dated 447 BC in the New7Wonders list).
won.mausoleum.t: Tomb of Mausolus, finished about 351 BC by Satyros and Pythius; brought down by earthquakes between the twelfth and fifteenth centuries.
won.colossus.t: Chares of Lindos's bronze Helios, raised in 292–280 BC and toppled by an earthquake in 226 BC.
won.lighthouse.t: Built about 280 BC under the Ptolemies; destroyed by earthquakes between 1303 and 1480, and its stones found underwater in 1994.
won.petra.t: The rock-cut Nabataean city in Jordan, dated AD 40 in the New7Wonders list.
won.pantheon.t: Hadrian's domed temple in Rome, rebuilt in 118–128.
won.teotihuacan.n: The Pyramid of the Sun, Teotihuacan
won.teotihuacan.t: The great pyramid of Teotihuacan, raised about AD 200.
won.hagia-sophia.t: Justinian's great church in Constantinople, finished in 537; later a mosque and a museum.
won.chichen-itza.t: The Maya city of Yucatán, dated AD 600 in the New7Wonders list; the pyramid of Kukulcan came later.
won.dome-of-the-rock.t: The Umayyad shrine on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem, completed in 692.
won.cordoba-mosque.t: Begun in 785 under the Umayyads of al-Andalus; later made a cathedral.
won.borobudur.t: The stepped Buddhist monument in central Java, built between about 760 and 830.
won.great-zimbabwe.t: The stone city of the Shona, begun in the eleventh century.
won.angkor-wat.t: The Khmer temple-city, begun about 1113; the Bayon was added at Angkor in 1181 under Jayavarman VII.
won.notre-dame.t: Begun in 1163 on the Île de la Cité and largely complete by 1260; burnt on 15 April 2019 and reopened in December 2024.
won.chartres.t: The Gothic cathedral rebuilt after the fire of 1194.
won.moai.t: The stone figures of Rapa Nui, dated about 1250 in the New7Wonders list.
won.timbuktu.t: The mosques and libraries of the Mali trading city, dated 1327 in the New7Wonders list.
won.alhambra.t: The Nasrid palace above Granada, dated 1333 in the New7Wonders list.
won.great-wall.t: The Ming wall from 1368 onward is the Great Wall that stands today; earlier walls go back to the Qin.
won.forbidden-city.t: The Ming palace in Beijing, built in the 1420s.
won.machu-picchu.t: The Inca estate above the Urubamba, dated about 1450.
won.st-basils.n: St Basil's Cathedral and Red Square
won.st-basils.t: The cathedral on Red Square, completed in 1561 under Ivan IV; the New7Wonders list dates the Kremlin and Red Square to that year.
won.st-peters.t: Begun in the 1500s and consecrated in the 1620s; the largest church of the Renaissance and Baroque.
won.kiyomizu.t: The wooden temple above Kyoto, rebuilt in 1633.
won.taj-mahal.t: Shah Jahan's tomb for Mumtaz Mahal at Agra, begun in 1632 and dated 1643 in the New7Wonders list.
won.versailles.t: Louis XIV's palace, enlarged from a hunting lodge from the 1660s.
won.potala.t: The palace of the Dalai Lamas above Lhasa, built in the 1690s.
won.winter-palace.t: Rastrelli's Baroque palace on the Neva, built in 1754–1762; it houses the Hermitage.
won.westminster.t: The Houses of Parliament, rebuilt from 1840.
won.crystal-palace.t: Paxton's glass hall for the Great Exhibition of 1851; it was rebuilt at Sydenham and burnt down in 1936.
won.neuschwanstein.t: Ludwig II's castle in the Bavarian Alps, begun in 1869.
won.sagrada-familia.t: Gaudí's basilica in Barcelona, in his hands from 1884 and still unfinished.
won.statue-of-liberty.t: Bartholdi's statue in New York harbour, dedicated in 1886.
won.eiffel-tower.t: Built in 1887–1889 for the Paris Exposition.
won.christ-redeemer.t: The statue above Rio de Janeiro, completed in 1931.
won.sydney-opera.t: Jørn Utzon's shells on Bennelong Point, opened in 1973.
won.burj-khalifa.t: The tallest building in the world, opened in Dubai in 2010.
